Sam — thanks for the note and the attachments. We're happy to run a technical session. High level answers up front so your team can triage: 

1) BYOK flows we support for private/VPC:
   - Customer-managed HSM (KMIP / AWS CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM): customer holds root key material in their HSM; Redwood is provisioned with wrapped key handles and uses an ephemeral unwrap at runtime via TLS-authenticated unseal agents. No raw key material is stored in Redwood-managed storage.
   - Customer-supplied wrapped key blobs (offline BYOK): For air-gapped or restricted setups FintekCo can deliver a wrapped blob that Redwood imports into a sealed keystore; import is cryptographically auditable and requires operator attestation.

2) Escrow / sealed-key bridge pattern:
   - We support an encrypted escrow archive (sealed with customer's asymmetric key) stored in customer-controlled object storage or an operator escrow vault. The archive contains the minimum material to reconstruct long-term keys and is only retrievable with multi-party attestation.
   - Recovery requires explicit operator playbook: role-based approval, MFA-stamped audit, and a time-locked release window.

3) Operator controls & anti-exfiltration:
   - All unwrap/unseal occurs inside a hardened runtime container with restricted syscalls and chrooted file system for private deploys.
   - KMS operations are logged in an immutable audit stream (signed tokens) that can be pushed to customer SIEM.

Proposed next steps: 30–45 minute technical deep-dive with Soojin (security) + Aditya (infra) — we can cover: topology options (KMIP vs wrapped blobs), network controls (private peering, restricted egress), unseal playbook, and escrow rehearsal. I've attached a short 2-page pre-read we put together for similar customers.

Ben / Aditya — quick internal notes ahead of the call with FintekCo. Pulling these into the meeting to make sure we don't promise anything we can't audit:

- Escrow archive: recommend we require customer-side asymmetric wrapping (customer KMS holds the private key). The archive we store should be immutable and versioned; retrieval must require 2 internal approvers + one customer approver (email + OIDC assertion). That gives an auditable multi-party gate.

- Runtime unseal: for customer-managed HSM we should insist on a short-lived unwrap token that is only valid for the host boot window (e.g., 10 minutes). Token minting to be gated by attestation of the host (TPM quote or cloud instance identity).

- Operator access: no single operator should be able to perform an unseal or retrieve escrow. Implement temporary operator sessions with ephemeral credentials and record session transcript (keystroke-level logs optional per contract).

- Key rotation: support automated rotation schedules with re-encapsulation of escrow. For customers that need manual rotations (regulatory cadence) provide an exportable rotation report (signed by our key and customer's key).

I also flagged a short checklist for the infra diagrams that Aditya can bring: network ACLs for KMS endpoints, private CA for inter-host TLS, and egress filter policy to prevent outbound key material exfil.

I'll join the FintekCo call — suggest we accept the Wed 14 May 09:00 PT slot.

— Soojin
